One uninterrupted live-action opera shot, continuing the exact incoming frame with the SAME LOCKED WIDE audience camera. <Picture 1> is canonical Celes/Maria: preserve the approved real adult woman's face, blonde ponytail with blue bow, natural beige skin, ivory satin gown with blue trim and the same red rose bouquet. The incoming frame supplies current motion and pose: she is in three-quarter/profile toward the existing SCREEN-RIGHT curtain, bouquet supported by her RIGHT hand at waist height, LEFT forearm offered toward that curtain with palm slightly upward. Start in this exact pose; do not restart the invitation or jump to a frontal pose.
The existing English opera recording is in an instrumental interlude. She listens with relaxed lips, without invented dialogue or vowel-mouthing. No one answers her invitation. Her goal changes from reaching outward to gathering the memory of her absent beloved. During the first few seconds her gaze lingers on the right wing, then lowers to the real flowers. Her left wrist softly turns inward and that free hand slowly returns to the SAME bouquet stems while the right hand continues supporting their weight. Show a single continuous finger closure, without hand overlap, floating roses or a new bouquet.
In the middle of the shot her eyes redirect toward the audience before her head and shoulders unwind in a small balanced turn from right profile toward the established near-frontal stance. Her feet stay planted behind the same foreground battlement, no walking, sliding or full spin. Now BOTH hands support the bouquet as she slowly lifts it from waist level to the lower sternum; roses remain below the chin, never covering her face. Her arms and the weighted satin fabric respond naturally and independently. No repeated lowering/lifting, no renewed hand invitation, no flower throw.
In the final third she looks down at the roses briefly, draws a measured breath, then raises her eyes toward the distant audience-left horizon, retaining the bouquet near her heart. Her sorrow becomes a composed decision to continue. Let this gaze rise, subtle shoulder recovery and settling fingers develop through the final seconds; no frozen tail, bow, smile for applause or ending. This prepares the next vocal phrase, not a finale.
Exactly one woman remains visible. No partner, silhouette, hand, shadow, audience movement or object enters the right curtain or painted background. Preserve the exact stone stage, blue painted moonlit backdrop, right red velvet curtain, actor scale, camera axis, perspective, foreground occlusion and steady exposure. No new architecture or light. Neutral soft white on beige skin and ivory cloth; blue remains in the backdrop and dress trim. No magenta or pink skin wash, pulsing, flashing, glow or bloom. Real human anatomy, fingers, ponytail, physical satin and stable face. No cuts, dissolves, zoom, camera movement, closeup, subtitles, new Foley, invented voice or replacement music.
